Noise, checked against the exact answer

Five channels (bit flip, phase flip, depolarizing, amplitude damping, two-qubit depolarizing), readout error and a gate-noise model, each run as one random operator per run. One run is one noisy outcome; the average of many is the density matrix. Here a Bell pair through depolarizing noise on one qubit: {{t250.x1}} seeded runs per point against the exact curve (1 − p). The largest gap is {{t250.x2:.1f}} standard errors. {{t250.x3}} noisy circuits (up to 3 qubits) were compared to a density-matrix calculation over {{t250.x4}} runs each: worst z-scores {{t250.x5}}. Readout error, which flips the reported bit and not the state, is checked as a binomial (z = {{t250.x6:.1f}} on measured bits, {{t250.x7:.1f}} on samples, {{t250.x8:.1f}} when asymmetric). Doubling a probability on purpose is caught at z = {{t250.x9}}.

dm 2 keeps the whole density matrix, so one run is the exact answer, not a sample. The same Bell pair through depolarizing noise (p = 1/4) has purity {{t258.x1:.6f}} and trace {{t258.x2:.6f}}; the formula (1−p)² + p²/3 gives {{t258.x3:.6f}}. The curve is the purity against p: cancho, Qiskit and the formula agree to {{t258.x4:.0e}}. {{t258.x5}} density-matrix circuits (all channels, every gate, measurement) match Qiskit’s DensityMatrix. Up to 10 qubits: the matrix is stored as a state of twice as many.

The same circuits on {{t271.x1}} qubits, whole process for qsim (start, parse, run) against Aer’s run alone. Built with LLVM, qsim runs at {{t271.x2:.1f}}–{{t271.x3:.1f}}× the speed of Aer on one core, and at {{t271.x4:.1f}}–{{t271.x5:.1f}}× the speed of Aer on all four (1 is level; Aer’s time divided by ours). Cranelift, the default backend, is 3–6× slower than LLVM, so use --backend llvm for large circuits. A {{t271.x6}}-qubit state takes {{t271.x7:.0f}} MiB of {{t271.x8:.0f}}. The exact density matrix, once the weak spot (7× slower than Aer’s at 8 qubits), now takes {{t271.x9:.1f}}× Aer’s time there: its channels are single passes. Written in C with the same loops, three of the kernels run within {{t271.x10:.2f}}–{{t271.x11:.2f}}× of qsim’s time on the same compiler backend: the language is not the limit, memory and parallelism are. A JSON file describes a device: a depolarizing rate per qubit for one-qubit gates, per pair for two-qubit gates, and asymmetric readout error per qubit (a true 1 is misread more often than a true 0). tools/qprofile.cho (cancho) turns it into {{t284.x1}} operations and puts them in front of a circuit; qsim still reads only standard input. Below, a 5-qubit GHZ state through example-5q (invented numbers of a realistic size, not a real machine) on the density matrix: fidelity {{t284.x2:.4f}}, purity {{t284.x3:.4f}}. The bars are the exact outcome probabilities (readout error acts on top, when measuring). It matches a Qiskit calculation made from the JSON to 1e-12.

A qubit that waits decays. coher q T1 T2 gives it coherence times in nanoseconds; wait q ns idles it, and time1 / time2 make every gate take time, during which its qubits relax too. The channel is amplitude damping plus dephasing, sampled by trajectories or exact on the density matrix. Below, T1 = {{t290.x1}} µs and T2 = {{t290.x2}} µs: the chance a qubit is still 1, and the coherence of |+⟩, against waiting time. cancho, Qiskit Aer’s own thermal-relaxation channel and the formulas agree to {{t290.x3:.0e}}. {{t290.x4}} idle-noise circuits match Qiskit; a sampled GHZ circuit with gate times matches the exact density matrix within statistics.

sched starts every gate as soon as its qubits are free, and a qubit that finishes early idles (and relaxes) until its partner is ready. Below, qubit 0 starts as 1 and does nothing while a chain of cx gates runs on two other qubits: its chance of still being 1 follows exp(−t/T1) (T1 = {{t296.x1}} µs). Without sched it stays at exactly 1. Six random 14-gate circuits on 4 qubits, with different T1, T2 and gate times per qubit and pair, agree with Qiskit’s own ASAP scheduler (for the start times) and Aer’s relaxation channel to {{t296.x2:.0e}}; the same circuits without sched are at least {{t296.x3:.0e}} away, so the check can tell. Measurements and noise operations take no time; barrier waits for every qubit, and a sample or the final output implies one.

The calibration {{t315.x1}} published on {{t315.x2}} (the snapshot that ships with qiskit-ibm-runtime; no account, no live machine) is read into a profile by tools/qcalib.cho (cancho) (below: T1 and T2 in µs, the depolarizing probability p kept for one-qubit gates, readout error 0→1 and 1→0; cx time and error). Its T1, T2, gate times, readout and gate errors are all there. One conversion matters: IBM’s gate error already contains the decay during the gate, and the simulator adds that decay itself, so it is taken out first (for {{t315.x3}} of {{t315.x4}} pairs the T1/T2 decay alone exceeds the published error, so they get no extra depolarizing noise). {{t315.x5}} numbers were re-derived from the raw file by another route. Two circuits of native gates run through the profile on 7 qubits land within {{t315.x6:.0e}} (trace distance) of Qiskit Aer’s noise model built from the same snapshot, while the noise itself moves the state by {{t315.x7:.2f}}–{{t315.x8:.2f}}; leaving the idle decay out, or using the published error as is, is {{t315.x9:.0f}}–{{t315.x10:.0f}} times worse.

The noise model above, built only from a device’s published calibration, was run on the mirror circuits (a circuit followed by its inverse, which ought to return all zeros) that IBM’s {{t900.x1}} ran on {{t900.x2}}: {{t900.x3}} runs of up to {{t900.x4}} cz gates, {{t900.x5}} shots each. The exact density matrix is within {{t900.x6:.3f}} of what the device measured (total-variation distance from all zeros), close but not exact: a chi-square test (cancho-stats) at {{t900.x13}} shots tells the model from the device on every run. On {{t900.x7}} it is not: over {{t900.x8}} runs the device’s error was {{t900.x9:.1f}}–{{t900.x10:.1f}} times the model’s, and the calibration changed by more than the device did, so there the model is not reliable: most of the error traces to one qubit that read wrongly several times as often as its published calibration said (fitting that qubit’s read-out error brought the model within sampling noise of the device on circuits left out of the fit, for that run only). One qubit of {{t900.x11}} read 1 in {{t900.x12:.0f}}% of idle shots while its published calibration looked healthy; scripts/hw_spike.py now reads the qubits it will use before a run and refuses broken ones. One day, two devices, small circuits.

Noise that depends on the gate type, crosstalk between neighbouring qubits, leakage and non-Pauli two-qubit noise are not built; the model is depolarizing noise plus idle decay, at a rate per qubit or pair. A Toffoli has neither a duration nor a noise rate.
